meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law statutory foundation with Common Law-derived commercial and maritime adaptations, including trust and securities law)

Panama-Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty and Tax Treaty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama AML/CFT/CFP framework), as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 and related amendments; Executive Decree No. 363 of 5 August 2015; Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Ley 32 de 1998 and Ley 47 de 2013; Ley 70 de 2019 establishing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF); implementing regulations issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and competent supervisory bodies.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the Private Interest Foundation maintains third-party privacy; RBF beneficial-owner filings are accessible to competent AML/supervisory authorities and not publicly searchable; nominee mechanisms are permitted subject to full statutory disclosure to the registered agent)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, foundation council members, authorized signatories, and close associates against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Kingdom consolidated list, and Panamanian national databases; mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons under FATF Recommendations and UAF guidance; risk-based customer due diligence is required before acceptance of the foundation engagement and must be refreshed on change of UBO/controller or at least annually for the Low_Risk_Standard banking tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá online services portal (www.registro-publico.gob.pa), including name availability consultation and formal name reservation through a licensed notary or registered agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official foundation documents are prepared in Spanish; the foundation name may be expressed in Spanish or a foreign language using the Latin alphabet, provided it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; transliteration into Spanish for the public registry index is required for non-Spanish names; the name must include a Legal form indicator such as 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' and must not imply a corporate form inconsistent with the Private Interest Foundation structure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The incorporating counsel or registered agent files a preliminary name availability request with the Registro Público de Panamá. If the name is rejected, the requesting party may file a motion for reconsideration within five business days, with supporting evidence of distinctiveness and relevant search reports. If reaffirmed, an administrative appeal (apelación) may be filed with the Director General of the Registro Público within ten business days. A final adverse administrative decision may be challenged before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within two calendar months. The applicant may concurrently reserve a new name before expiration of the current reservation or re-file the desired name after a 30-day cooling-off period. All appeal and replacement filings should be notarized and submitted through the same registered agent or attorney of record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Panama Private Interest Foundation must maintain a statutory registered office at the physical office of its Panamanian registered agent; a virtual or mailbox-only address is not acceptable for service of process or statutory existence. For the airline inflight catering kitchen, the operational facility must be a physical and licensed airport-adjacent premises; no virtual office can satisfy MINSA/AAC food-safety or aviation-security requirements, though flexible administrative and dispatch functions may use hybrid arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: moderate annual probability of approximately 25-35% for physical AML/commercial-substance inspection of the registered office; elevated probability of approximately 45-55% for unannounced food-safety and aeronautical-compliance inspections by MINSA, Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil, and airport security authorities at the catering kitchen premises, given the bonded inflight-meal delivery scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended; Articles 1–25 (formation, patrimony, Foundation Council, registration, and supervision).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capitalization under Law 25, but the Foundation Charter must declare an initial patrimony/endowment adequate for its purpose; a pre-formation escrow account is not legally required. An initial endowment of US$10,000 is adopted by the Founder and subscribed in the First Board Resolution to satisfy banking and AML counterparty expectations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Founder hereby subscribes an initial endowment of US$10,000 to the Foundation's patrimony, which may be increased by subsequent contributions; and it is further RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation shall be established at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama; and it is further RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed to the Foundation Council: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Member, each to serve indefinite terms; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Council is authorized to undertake all filings, open bank accounts, and execute all instruments necessary for the Foundation's incorporation, taxation, and operational licensing under the Republic of Panama and for the business of airline inflight catering.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the Public Registry's online system, identifying the entity type as Private Interest Foundation and providing the proposed official Spanish name. Upon approval, prepare the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública Constitutiva) in notarizable draft form, including by-laws, initial patrimony, Foundation Council composition, and registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited terms, file a second name reservation with alternative names within 5 business days; no fee penalty beyond reservation fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with final charter text and founder identification. The notary reads the deed, verifies the founder's signature, and produces the Escritura Pública number. Notarization is required before any registry submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any typographical or legal inconsistency by preparing an addendum (aclaración) or re-executing the deed before the same notary without re-starting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Public Registry's Foundation Section along with the payment receipt. The Registry examines legal compliance, issues a registrar's certificate (Inscripción), and assigns the Foundation's unique legal entity registry number.
required_dossiers: Signed cover letter identifying the president of the Foundation Council
Copy of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'nota de defectos' (defect notice), cure the described deficiencies in writing within 5 business days, attaching corrected deed pages or supplementary agreements; otherwise the application is archived and must be re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gaceta Oficial Digital – Government Printing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registry inscription, obtain an authenticated copy of the Foundation deed from the Public Registry and submit it to the Oficial Mayor de Gaceta. The publication provides judicial and third-party effectiveness of the Foundation's existence and the Council members' powers.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registry inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or materially incorrect, request republication with corrected text; payment of editing fee covers a corrective insert.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Municipal Registration (RUC and Patent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sistema Único de Negocio (SUNO) – Municipality of Panama and Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through SUNO for the Unified Taxpayer Registry (RUC) and municipal operating license (Aviso/Patente). Submit the registered Foundation Charter, president's identification, and proof of physical facility address for the inflight catering kitchen. Obtain business tax registration number and municipal patent certificate.
required_dossiers: Kitchen lease or property title documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SUNO rejects due to incomplete documentation or address verification, request a technical inspection, correct the dossier, and refile online; an appeal may be filed with the Municipal Tax Office within 5 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Food Safety and Environmental Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección de Regulación de Alimentos; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); SINAPROC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to MINSA a sanitary operation permit application for the inflight catering kitchen, including HACCP plan, facility blueprints, and waste management statement. Concurrently file an environmental registration/assessment with MiAMBIENTE if required. Obtain SINAPROC fire-safety approval. These permits authorize commercial production and ramp delivery of airline meals.
required_dossiers: HACCP and food safety management plan
Kitchen facility layout and structural drawings
Wastewater discharge and solid waste management plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA identifies deficient HACCP or physical structure issues, arrange a reinspection within 5 business days after remediating the cited deficiencies; await a maximum 10-day extension before formally appealing to the MINSA Regional Director.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Regulación de Alimentos; with technical coordination of the Autoridad Panameña de Seguridad de Alimentos (AUPSA) for imported inputs and food safety inspections.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Operación para Fábrica de Alimentos / Comedor de Catering (Sanitary Operating Permit for Food Manufacturing / Catering Kitchen)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III (Registro Ambiental) for food preparation facilities with daily meal output below 10,000 and manageable waste loads; Category II (Evaluación Ambiental Preliminar) required if wastewater discharge exceeds 200 m³/day or if facility is within 200 m of protected areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo 75 de 2011 (wastewater discharge parameters) and Reglamento Técnico DGNTI-COPANIT on industrial wastewater; VOC emissions from cooking processes must not exceed 50 mg/m³; solid waste must be segregated per Ley 8 de 2014 and food waste rendered or disposed via an authorized sanitary landfill.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Aprobación de SINAPROC (fire safety certification) covering commercial kitchen fire suppression, hangar/ramp vehicle parking, and emergency egress; structural load inspection by the Municipal Engineering Bureau for catering equipment; workplace safety clearance by the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) for occupational hazard prevention and food handlers' health credentials.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama; electronic taxpayer portal at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (SITIO e-filing system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must be duly registered in the Public Registry of Panama, appoint a resident agent, obtain a Notary-certified extract of the foundation charter, apply for a digital signature token, and then register online or in person with the DGI Single Registry of Taxpayers (RUC). The application must include the foundation deed, registered address, description of the taxable activity (airline inflight catering and ramp delivery), and the resident agent's identification. The DGI will inscribe the PIF for income tax and ITBMS (VAT) and issue the statutory RUC number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available under Panamanian law. The Private Interest Foundation is treated as a separate juridical person subject to entity-level taxation on Panama-source income only. Foreign-source income is outside the territorial tax base; qualifying export revenues are zero-rated for ITBMS. A small-taxpayer simplified regime may be elected only for persons with annual gross receipts not exceeding USD 36,000.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – VAT-equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 36,000 annual taxable turnover for compulsory regular ITBMS registration in the general regime; persons at or below this threshold may be inscribed under the small-taxpayer regime subject to a reduced rate of 2% on taxable sales with no input VAT credit. Once engaged in commercial operations in Panama, obtaining RUC and ITBMS registration is mandatory even if actual turnover has not yet reached the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates phased electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) through the DGI's SITIO system. Taxpayers with annual gross turnover above USD 5 million must transmit invoices in real time or within 24 hours for DGI digital validation and assignment of a unique financial fiscal stamp; other taxpayers must adopt e-invoicing according to the DGI schedule. Export invoices must carry the zero-rated ITBMS feeder code and reference the export customs document. Fiscal printing equipment remains acceptable for non-mandated taxpayers, but electronic issuance is the long-term statutory standard.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Meals, beverages, and inflight supplies produced in a bonded catering kitchen and physically delivered to an aircraft departing from Panamanian territory qualify as exports of goods for ITBMS purposes when the goods leave the customs territory under an authorized customs procedure. Ancillary ramp-handling and logistics services directly linked to the offshore flight are zero-rated when they are performed for the benefit of a non-resident carrier and substantiated as consumed outside Panama. Eligibility requires that the supplier holds an export license from the National Customs Authority (ANA), maintains separate accounting for export sales, and submits periodic ITBMS declarations containing a zero-rated schedule. Direct proof of departure and receipt outside Panama must be maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera) electronically validated by the National Customs Authority (ANA)
Master and house air waybills evidencing the aircraft dispatch from Panama
Signed proof of delivery / ramp handover receipt from the receiving airline or authorized ground handler
Commercial invoice and packing list explicitly identifying the zero-rated ITBMS treatment
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment of the export invoice by the non-resident airline
Flight schedule or departure report confirming the aircraft's registration and destination outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA jointly scrutinize zero-rating claims, with a general tax audit statute of limitations of five years. If export evidence is found false, incomplete, or inconsistent, the zero rating is annulled retroactively, resulting in immediate assessment of the 7% ITBMS, monthly late surcharges of 1.5%, and fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the omitted tax, together with criminal penalties for customs fraud. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may trigger recharacterization of the unrepatriated amount as a Panama-source taxable gain subject to 25% corporate income tax and additional non-compliance surcharges for late filing and payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Not applicable - Panama does not have a central bank and does not maintain a national foreign-exchange administration. The monetary framework is full dollarization and the U.S. dollar is legal tender. The principal banking regulatory authority is the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP). The state-owned Banco Nacional de Panama acts solely as a commercial and fiscal agent, not as a monetary authority or exchange-control body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under full de facto dollarization, so the current account and capital account are completely convertible in U.S. dollars. There are no central-bank exchange controls, no prior approval for cross-border payment instructions, and no profit-repatriation license requirements. The Panamanian balboa exists only as coins pegged 1:1 to the USD and does not create convertibility friction. Profit remittances and foundation beneficiary distributions can be made freely through SBP-licensed banks. The principal obstacle is not FX but the territorial tax framework: Panamanian-source commercial profits are subject to corporate income tax and dividend equalization rules, whereas income sourced outside Panama is outside the territorial tax net if the PIF does not operate a Panamanian-source commercial establishment. A passive PIF can remit distributions to beneficiaries without an FX conversion or exchange-control filing; an onshore catering kitchen would need to account for Panamanian-source revenue as taxable income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory deadline for the repatriation of export or trade revenue. Receipts from airline in-flight catering contracts, including wire payments from non-resident airlines, may be held indefinitely in USD in Panamanian bank accounts or foreign accounts. The only compliance requirements are the SBP and Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) anti-money-laundering reporting rules, including currency transaction reporting for cash above USD 10,000 and suspicious-transaction monitoring for electronic wires; these do not amount to exchange controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. – Panama Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for use as the primary treasury account; Medium as an auxiliary low-value collection and disbursement channel. Offshore digital EMIs and non-bank financial service providers such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex are not licensed as banks by the SBP and are not treated as Panamanian banks. They cannot issue commercial letters of credit, hold regulatory deposit status, or serve as the principal escrow account for PIF capital. Some EMIs can process inbound/outbound USD transfers through local correspondent banks, but account opening for a PIF by an offshore EMI will still require the full beneficial-ownership file, apostilled foundation charter, notarized Foundation Council resolution, and passport verification. Balances held with an unlicensed EMI are not protected by Panama's deposit framework and should be limited to low-value disbursement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default expectation. Panamanian tier-1 banks generally require at least one member of the Foundation Council and the Resident Agent to attend an in-person onboarding interview at a bank branch. A fully remote account opening is rarely available for a Private Interest Foundation. Where video-identity KYC is permitted by a bank's compliance policy, the client must still provide apostilled formation documents, a notarized Council resolution, a certificate of good standing, passport copies of all signatories, and a sworn source-of-wealth statement. For PIFs, the compliance officer normally mandates a face-to-face meeting to confirm the identity, business rationale, and economic substance of the foundation before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation opacity: a Panama Law 25 PIF has no public register of beneficiaries, and some bank compliance teams classify this structure as high-risk for concealment or misuse as an offshore shell.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled foundation charter and official registration certificate; current registered-agent certificate; notarized Foundation Council resolution authorizing the account and naming the treasury signatories; a complete beneficial-ownership schedule identifying settlor, guardian, council members, and beneficiaries; a source-of-wealth questionnaire with income and net-worth documentation; and a written business-rationale letter explaining that the PIF is the holding vehicle for an airline in-flight catering kitchen and aviation concession operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected shell activity: the applicant is a PIF rather than a manufacturing operating company, which may raise doubts about whether any real catering kitchen, staff, or physical facilities exist.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed master catering supply agreement with one or more recognized air carriers; airport concession license or long-term lease for the catering kitchen; photographs of the facility, production flow, and blast-chilling equipment; payroll lists of on-site kitchen personnel; inbound and delivery temperature logs; customs and sanitary import permits for meal components; and audited or management-reviewed financial statements showing kitchen operating expenses and aviation receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border cash-flow pattern: recurring monthly ACH or SWIFT MT103 payments from non-resident airline clients without clear invoice references, or with rapid pass-through of funds to third-country suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice-level accounts receivable aging; per-flight order and delivery records cross-referencing the airline invoice numbers; IATA certificates and air-operator certificates of the airline clients; SWIFT sender confirmations from the airline treasury systems; bank statement annotations showing the underlying catering contract; and a documented flow chart from airline payment to supplier settlement demonstrating that all funds are applied to genuine meal-production and logistics obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial endowment sourced from a non-resident settlor or from a third-party corporate account in a round-dollar amount, prompting source-of-funds and possible third-party funding suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled foundation endowment deed; bank reference letter from the settlor's home-country institution; three years of audited financial statements or tax returns for the settlor or contributing company; a group corporate tree showing the ultimate beneficial owner; and a declaration, signed under penalty of perjury, that the endowment was derived from lawful aviation, hotel, or food-service business proceeds and not from cash, cryptocurrency, or undisclosed third parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial foundation capital must be wired as a serial SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident settlor to the PIF's designated Capital Escrow Account at the Panamanian bank. The payment narrative should state Endowment to Private Interest Foundation under Panama Law 25, with no commercial invoice reference. The beneficiary account field must match the foundation name exactly as shown in the foundation charter and bank account opening documents. For commercial receivables from airline catering clients, the remitting airline or its treasury vendor should send USD by SWIFT MT103 with payment reason Flight catering invoice [number], catering contract [reference], and the airline's IATA billing code. Panama has no central-bank purpose-code taxonomy, so the receiving bank relies on the SWIFT narrative for AML classification. Verification procedures include OFAC screening, PEP and sanctions checks, account-title matching, and comparison of the payment reason against the PIF's declared business purpose. There is no exchange-control filing or FX conversion because the funds remain in USD. The Capital Escrow Account must be segregated from the Operational Account until the Foundation Council passes a written resolution authorising use of the endowment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border supplier payments should be executed by SWIFT MT103 serial or cover payment from the PIF's Operational Account. Payment references must include the supplier invoice number, purchase order, and catering-kitchen import document reference. For high-value imported meal components and galley equipment, the preferred clearing rail is a commercial documentary letter of credit issued by the Panamanian bank through SWIFT MT700/MT710, payable at sight or on a 30-to-60-day tenor against presentation of commercial invoice, airway bill, cold-chain certificate, packing list, and sanitary certificate. Local recurring payments for airport concession fees, rent, utilities, and monthly wages should be settled through Panama's local ACH clearing mechanism or same-day bank transfer; because Panama has no central-bank RTGS, large same-day USD values are finally settled through the banks' correspondent accounts in the U.S. clearing system. Every outbound payment must be supported by an economic-substance record demonstrating that the PIF is executing genuine trade, meal-production, or logistics disbursements rather than functioning as a pass-through treasury shell.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/JPY) with SBP-licensed Panamanian banks, executed under a bank master agreement or ISDA/CSA and limited to documented catering import or concession liabilities.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for counterpart currencies without an active onshore USD settlement market, booked by the Panamanian bank's offshore head office or an OECD-market counterparty and settled in U.S. dollars.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) and long-dated cross-currency interest-rate swaps for financing structures denominated in EUR or GBP, subject to explicit Foundation Council authorization and full audit trail.
Plain-vanilla interest-rate derivatives on USD borrowings used solely to fix floating-rate financing costs; speculative derivative positions are outside the permissible treasury policy for the PIF.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation tax payment (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year; no extension is granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 25 late-payment surcharge plus statutory interest on the unpaid USD 300; failure for seven consecutive years is a cause for administrative strike-off by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta, Form 120) for Panama-source catering revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following the close of the calendar fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing surcharge and adjusted interest on any tax due; repeated failure to file may trigger DGI enforcement actions, fiscal integration measures, and criminal sanctions for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership record confirmation (confirmed in the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 or within 30 days after any change in foundations, protectors, foundation council members, or beneficiaries.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to USD 1,000 for inaccurate or untimely UBO information; the tax compliance certificate (Paz y Salvo) may be refused until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of municipal operation permit for the airport bonded catering kitchen (Renovación de Aviso de Operación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tesorería Municipal / Municipality of Panama or where registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of the initial Aviso de Operación; generally due in January of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal surcharges, interest, and temporary closure or suspension of the operation permit if the renewal is not made.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory for taxpayers classified as 'large taxpayers' by the DGI or when annual Panama-source gross revenue exceeds USD 1,500,000, or when total assets exceed USD 3,000,000; for smaller entities a licensed accountant's reviewed financial statement is sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Panama for large taxpayers; IFRS for SMEs or Panamanian GAAP for middle/small catering operators; airport and civil-aviation concession contracts may prescribe additional accounting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Private Interest Foundation has no shareholders; the registered agent must review and update the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry each year by March 31, reporting any changes in the founder's reserved rights, foundation council members, protectors, and beneficiaries within 30 days of the change through supplementary foundation documents.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Foundation Purposes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system. A Private Interest Foundation is taxable only on income sourced in Panama; foreign-source income is outside Panamanian corporate income tax and therefore carries an effective 0% rate. Airline in-flight catering revenue derived from meal production and direct ramp delivery physically performed in Panama is Panamanian-source income. No statutory tax holiday or preferential zone rate applies to ISIC 5621 airport catering operations under the standard territorial regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 410 (Declaración de Renta Anual de Personas Jurídicas) filed via the Panama Dirección General de Ingresos e-Tax 2.0 electronic portal (Sistema de Gestión de Ingresos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual Form 410; monthly advance income tax payments are made separately on Formulario 510 during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the last day of the third month following the fiscal-year end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the filing deadline is 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian tax identification number, exact legal name of the Private Interest Foundation, registered address, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register the PIF with the DGI to obtain its own RUC before filing. A non-resident founder must appoint a resident agent or registered agent with notarized power of attorney to execute the declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Ingresos Brutos Panameños (Gross Panamanian Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from Panamanian sources, including all catering service fees charged to airlines for in-flight meal production, galley loading, and ramp delivery within Panamanian airports.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue physically sourced in Panama. Exclude invoices for meals prepared outside Panama and any foreign-ramp or foreign-airline distribution activity not performed inside Panamanian territory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutorily allowed deductions: raw food and beverage costs, direct kitchen labor, leased kitchen and hangar space, utilities, fuel for delivery vehicles, airport access fees, insurance, depreciation of ovens and vehicles, and documented overhead proper to the catering activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only supportable deductions with invoices issued to the PIF's RUC are allowed. Foreign head-office expenses cannot be deducted unless the PIF maintains a taxable Panamanian permanent establishment with a proper cost allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 – Renta Neta Gravable (Net Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panamanian-source catering revenues less allowed deductions and allowable prior-year loss carryforwards, producing the net taxable base subject to the 25% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF with no Panamanian-source activity must enter zero in this box and maintain full evidence of the territorial source of all excluded foreign revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 19 – Impuesto Sobre la Renta (Income Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of net taxable income, reduced by monthly advance payments already made on Formulario 510, by withholding tax credits, and by any valid payments bearing DGI payment receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not credit foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income. Attach bank certificates or e-Tax generated receipts for all Panamanian advance tax payments claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Formulario 410 attracts a graduated surcharge of 5% per month of the tax due up to a statutory cap, compounded default interest on the unpaid balance, and administrative fines for continued non-compliance. Repeated or intentional non-filing of Panamanian-source catering income is prosecuted as tax evasion under Panama's Criminal Code and may expose the corporate assets to attachment and forced sale.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax when distributions are made from profits that have borne Panamanian corporate income tax; 20% withholding tax applies to dividends or beneficiary distributions made from profits that have not been subject to Panamanian corporate income tax. For a Private Interest Foundation, distributions of Panamanian-source catering profits to beneficiaries are treated as dividend-equivalent distributions for withholding purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke relief under a Panamanian double taxation agreement, the non-resident beneficiary or lender must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence from the competent authority of its jurisdiction of residence and submit it to the Panamanian withholding agent. The withholding agent must file the treaty relief request through the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal together with a Spanish-language sworn statement confirming the recipient is the beneficial owner and has no permanent establishment in Panama. Relief is allowed at source only where the applicable DTA expressly reduces the Panamanian statutory withholding rate; otherwise the full statutory rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panamanian withholding rates for payments to non-residents: 25% on gross royalties for the use of intellectual property exploited in Panama; 12.5% on gross interest paid on debt owed by a Panamanian resident payer to a non-resident lender, unless the lender is a licensed international banking corporation, in which case the interest may be exempt. Where a double taxation agreement applies, treaty rates for royalties and interest commonly reduce to 10% or 5% upon submission of valid tax residence certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where gross income exceeds PAB 3,000,000 and controlled transactions with related enterprises exceed PAB 1,000,000; Master File is mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds PAB 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations, implemented through Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 167 of 2021, impose substance requirements principally on entities deriving mobile or cross-border income under preferential regimes. In-flight catering physically performed from a Panamanian kitchen is not a relevant activity; nonetheless, the DGI may disregard the separate personality of a Private Interest Foundation if it operates as a shell without personnel, premises, or equipment. The PIF must maintain actual staff, kitchen facilities, delivery vehicles, and operational control over ramp logistics to defend its territorial tax treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of airline catering invoices, false reduction of gross receipts from bonded kitchen sales, fabrication of kitchen payroll and food-supplier deductions, or submission of materially false Formulario 410 declarations to evade Panamanian-source tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's Criminal Code penalizes tax evasion and fraud with imprisonment of two to five years; the tax authority may additionally assess the evaded tax, monthly default interest, and surcharges of up to 50% of the deficiency, followed by seizure and judicial auction of kitchen assets and delivery vehicles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, founder, and registered agent may be held personally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax. Courts may pierce the Private Interest Foundation's veil where it was used as a sham to evade tax; travel bans, restriction of movement, disqualification from serving as foundation agents, and imprisonment can follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Foundation / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an airport catering kitchen in name only, with no employees, no kitchen equipment, no delivery vehicles, and directing all airline contract wire receipts to offshore accounts while claiming Panamanian territorial exemptions or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard the foundation's separate legal status, re-characterize all catering revenue as Panamanian-source, disallow deductions, assess the full 25% corporate tax plus default interest and penalties, and impose fines for failure to maintain economic substance and registered beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members who knowingly operate the foundation without real economic activity face personal liability for assessed tax deficiencies. Travel bans may be imposed pending criminal investigation, and convictions for fraudulent use of legal persons can lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Private Interest Foundation to obscure the ultimate beneficial owner of catering profits, routing Aviation Contract Wire or Monthly ACH payments through accounts without filing beneficial ownership reports, or failing to cooperate with Panama's Financial Analysis Unit under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML regime authorizes fines of up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, suspension of the foundation's commercial license, confiscation of the funds involved, and criminal prosecution under money laundering statutes with sentences of five to twelve years of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and compliance officers face direct criminal responsibility, personal fines, travel bans, and extradition exposure when the foundation's financial infrastructure is deliberately used to conceal illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Related-Party Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in related-party transactions with foreign affiliates, inflating input costs from related catering suppliers, charging non-arm's-length management fees, or failing to prepare and file the mandatory Transfer Pricing Local File and Master File once the PAB thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may impose penalties equal to 1% of the adjusted related-party transaction value, recalculate the taxpayer's taxable income using the most appropriate arm's-length method, assess the resulting tax at 25%, and add default interest and late-filing surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve inaccurate transfer pricing documentation may be jointly liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties. In aggravated cases involving coordinated evasion through the foundation, personal civil restitution, travel bans, and criminal sanctions apply.
